title: Accounts docs
intro: Accounts is the sign-up and sign-in system of your own website and admin: one user list for your customers and your staff, with roles. Visitors sign in with the widget or with your own screens on the API; your server and our other products check their sign-ins offline with your website's public keys. Your website's tokens are in the Portal: open the website, then Install and tokens. The browser token is public and goes into your pages; the server token is secret and stays on your server.
localhost: Testing on your own computer: the browser token also works on pages served from localhost, *.localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1], on any port, over http or https. These pages use your website's real database, keys and providers, so the accounts made there are real. There is no test mode.
methods: Sign-in methods are features: Phone code (a code by SMS or WhatsApp), Phone + password, Email + password, Email code / magic link, Google, Apple and Facebook. Turn on the ones you want; the widget shows exactly those. Phone code and Phone + password share Settings → Phone numbers and codes: the phone format (default calling code and trunk prefix; an empty calling code means your business.json country's) and how codes go (the channel, the code length and how long a code lasts, the wait between codes and the hourly caps): numbers are kept as E.164, the way every product reads them, so +44 07700 900123, 0044 7700 900123, 447700900123 and 07700-900123 (with +44) are one number. Codes, magic links, password resets and invites are sent through Notifications: paste your website's Notifications server token into Connections. They go out with Accounts' default words (US English) until you write your own in Notifications (Settings → Templates; keys below, with the values each one gets); WhatsApp has no default words, so a code by WhatsApp needs your WhatsApp template approved at Meta (until then it fails as not set up, or goes by SMS when you set that fallback in Notifications). Phone + password's Forgot password sends accounts.phone_code on the phone channel (Settings → Phone numbers and codes); with Forgot password off, its link opens your own page (for example a WhatsApp chat). Without Notifications, those steps answer notifications_not_connected, except Forgot password: both Forgot password routes answer 202 at once whether or not the address has an account and whatever the send gives (a cooldown or cap sends nothing), and a reset link or code Notifications cannot send now is sent again right after later requests while it is valid. Reset links open the returnTo page on your website's domain, or on one of your hosts listed in resetHosts (for example your admin's own host, over https). Forgot password by email takes resetLimit requests per address per 15 minutes (default 3; 1 to 20), counted for every address whether or not it has an account; more answer 429 rate_limited. Email codes and phone codes each have their own limits in Settings (Email code / magic link, and Phone numbers and codes): they last codeMinutes (default 10), wait between sends (cooldownSeconds, default 30; refusal code_cooldown with retryAt), are capped per address and per website each hour (perHour, default 6, and websitePerHour, default 0 = no cap; code_limit), and a code is used up after codeTries wrong tries (default 5). Sign-in codes by phone may be limited to your countries (Phone code setting; country_not_allowed), and a new user without a name gets the newUserName template ({last4}: the number's last 4 digits). An email code, a magic link or a Google, Apple or Facebook sign-in opens only an account whose email address was proven (by an earlier code or link, a password reset, an invite, a social sign-in or staff entering it); an address typed but never proven (at a phone sign-up, in a role request or at an email + password sign-up) counts as unknown, so the sign-up that follows answers already_exists and that account is never opened. Forgot password by email sends its link only to a proven address or to the address the account was made with (an email + password sign-up, an email invite): for an address only typed on an account that signs in another way, it answers 202 as for an unknown address and sends nothing. A sign-in code from staff typed in the email code screen opens its user but proves no address.
social: Google, Apple and Facebook use your own app keys (Connections). Register the return address below with the provider. The widget opens the provider's page; the provider sends the person back to Accounts, which finds or creates the user and returns the browser to your page with a single-use code in the address fragment; the widget exchanges it for the sign-in.
signIns: A sign-in is a JWT signed with EdDSA (Ed25519) that lasts 15 minutes: iss is Accounts' address, aud is your website id, sub is the user id, and it carries name, email with email_verified, phone with phone_verified and, with Roles and permissions on, role and permissions (* = every permission). The widget renews it with the user's session (session length and remember me are set per role; defaults 1 day and 30 days). Verify it on your server with the public keys (no call per check), and paste the Accounts server token into other products so they trust sign-ins too. A password change ends the user's sessions made before it: every user answer (My account, the sign-in and renew answers, the server and Users widget views) carries passwordChangedAt (when the password was last set or changed, else null), My account and renewing refuse a session made before it with 401 signed_out (the device that changed its own password stays signed in), and a sign-in already issued ends within 15 minutes; if you keep sessions of your own, end those whose start (iat) is before passwordChangedAt. A sign-in only says who the user is: it never authorizes admin actions in any product — those need your server token or a ticket.
visitorApi: Headless: build your own screens on the visitor API with the browser token. Routes of a signed-in user also take the sign-in in the SS-Sign-In header. Your own server can make these visitor calls for a person with its server token and the person's network address in SS-Visitor-IP: sign-in, sign-up, forgot and reset password (for staff too, since nobody is signed in), the shopper's own account (/v1/me, with the shopper's SS-Sign-In) and GET /v1/fields/public. No staff sign-in is needed for them; staff work and configuration still need one. Sign-in and sign-up routes answer { status: signed_in, signIn, expiresAt, refreshToken, sessionExpiresAt, remember, user }, { status: two_step, challenge, expiresAt }, { status: two_step_setup, challenge, expiresAt, secret, otpauthUrl } or { status: pending }; the API reference below gives every route's body and answer. Keep the refresh token in the browser and renew with POST /v1/session/refresh: each renew answers a new refresh token; the old one presented again within 30 seconds (parallel requests, a retried renew) gets the same new pair, and later it ends the session (it was copied).
roles: One user list: every new sign-up gets the role for new sign-ups (Customer at first); GET /v1/users/count and /v1/users/counts?by=status|role count it with the list's filters (q, role, roles, permission, status, blocked, deletion, phone, phoneDigits, consent, tags, createdAfter). Users carry your own tags (for example VIP or Wholesale; up to 20 each, set with tags on POST and PATCH /v1/users, listed with their counts by GET /v1/users/tags, seen by staff only), and staff keep named saved views of the list's filters (GET, PUT and DELETE /v1/users/views/:key, PUT /v1/users/views { order }) that the Users widget opens in one click. On first use your website gets ready-made templates (Owner, Business manager, Product manager, Marketing manager, Support staff and Customer) with default permissions from Accounts, Chat, Notifications and Ecommerce; from then on they are your roles: change, copy or delete them (a deleted template stays deleted), and add your own (Settings: how many roles, default 100 and up to 200). Only two roles are system roles that cannot be deleted: Owner (every permission, rank 100) and the role for new sign-ups (signUp: true on one role, never Owner; choose another role to move it). Users of a deleted role get the role for new sign-ups. membership (on by default, off for Customer) shows the role on the user's own account as “Member since”. A role's permissions come from the products whose server tokens you pasted into Accounts (each product publishes its list), plus your own permission names (site:<name>). A role also sets two-step (optional or required), the session length and remember me, and: rank (a smaller number ranks higher: Owner is always 100 and every other role sits between 101 and 999; the templates start at Business manager 200, Product manager 300, Marketing manager 400, Support staff 500 and Customer 900), remember (ask, ask_ticked, always: no box, always remembered, or never: no box, never remembered, so the session ends when the browser closes and, on the server, at the latest after the longer of the session length and the remember-me days; a sign-in answers remember: false, so the widget keeps the session in sessionStorage and your server keeps it in a cookie without an expiry), methods (the sign-in methods its users may use; [] = all; others get method_refused), signIn (on, or paused: its users, and new sign-ups while the role for new sign-ups is paused, get sign_in_paused with your paused text, before any code is sent), logSignIns (sign-ins, failures with their IP, resets, recovery-code use and new recovery codes go to the activity log) and sessionRolling (false: a session ends at a fixed time after sign-in; true: each renewal moves its end to the session length, or the remember-me days, from then, so a session in use does not end). Your admin checks the user's role and permissions before it asks a product for a ticket.
rules: Sign-up rules (Approval / invite sign-up): open sign-up, invite only, or approval required, and which standard fields are required. Custom fields are set in the dashboard, in your order (Settings: how many fields, default 50 and up to 100, and choices per field, default 50 and up to 200): text, long text, number, date, one choice, several choices, yes/no, email address or web address, each with a help text and who sees it — the user edits it, the user only sees it (staff edit it), or only staff see it (never sent to the browser, nor in the user's data download, like your notes). Fields the user edits are asked at sign-up (the required ones) and shown in My account; staff see and edit every field in the Users widget and through /v1/users (custom), and a signed-in staff member lists them with GET /v1/fields. Your own sign-up and My account pages read the ones the user sees (not the staff-only ones) from GET /v1/fields/public, open to the browser and to your server with no sign-in. The data download carries the fields the user sees, and a required field is never left empty once asked. Profile settings (shown while any sign-in method is on): addresses per user (default 10, up to 50), keep at least one address, and the required address fields; addresses have a label (for example Home or Office), an area and one default address, and follow their country's format (one table shared with Ecommerce): the country is a picker kept as its ISO code (an address without one is in your business.json country), the form shows the country's parts in its order with its labels (State, Province, Prefecture, Emirate, ZIP code, PIN code …: widget texts address.<part>.<kind> you can rename), the region and postal code are required where the country requires them, no postal code is asked where a country has none, and the postal code must have the country's shape. Imported addresses keep their parts as they were (the country becomes its code). Security: password rules (a minimum length up to 128, a maximum length of 128 to 256 (default 256), at least one letter and one digit (off by default), the breached-password check, and the personal check that refuses the name, the email's local part or runs like 1234 or qwer; a refused password answers weak_password with the rule it breaks: too_short with minLength, too_long with maxLength, letter_and_digit, personal or breached), a fixed or growing lock after repeated wrong passwords, two-step codes or recovery codes (growing: 1 minute, doubling up to 60; two-step is refused while the lock lasts; after a quiet period with none, 24 hours by default, the earlier ones no longer count), a limit of tries per network and address per 15 minutes (the right password clears them; the lock mode, this limit and the personal check are the Passwords settings, shared by Email + password and Phone + password), two-step sign-in with recovery codes (a signed-in user replaces them with POST /v1/me/two-step/recovery-codes { code } or { recoveryCode }: a code from the app or one recovery code proves the step, the old codes stop working, wrong codes count toward the lock; My account has New recovery codes), risk checks against disposable email addresses (a built-in list of common disposable domains, your own refused domains, and the domains you always allow) and many accounts from one device or network, and consents (the answer each user gave, with its version and time).
dataRights: Download my data gives the user one single-use link (15 minutes) to everything Accounts and every product whose token you pasted keep about them. Delete my account waits for your approval in the Users admin widget (or for the days set in Settings), then erases the user here and in every connected product; a product that cannot be reached is asked again on later requests.
activity: Activity log copy: paste this website's Accounts server token into your other products; each one then sends every staff action to Accounts: who (with the acting user's role), what, the target and its label (for example an order number), what changed (values: codes, numbers and yes/no that your screens and the Activity widget put into words, or a product's short detail) and when — never message contents, secrets or addresses. Accounts' own log (GET /v1/activity) keeps what changed as values too, for example role.saved { change, permissions, twoStep, rank, signIn, signUp }, user.role_changed { from, to }, user.invited { role, delivery, days } and, for roles that log sign-ins, user.signed_in { ip, method } and user.sign_in_failed { ip, reason }. Read the copies with GET /v1/activity-copies?productId=&actor=&action=&target=&q=&from=&to= (newest first; action takes one action or several separated by commas, q searches labels, details, names and targets, from and to take an ISO-8601 time or a day in your business.json time zone) and count them with GET /v1/activity-copies/count and /v1/activity-copies/counts?by=productId|action|actor. Accounts' own log (users and roles, with each user's name or role as the label) is read with GET /v1/activity.
orders: Orders tab: paste the Ecommerce server token; My account then lists the user's last 20 orders from Ecommerce (GET /v1/customers/<userId>/orders on Ecommerce, with the server token you pasted): number, status (the status label your shop set) and total.
staff: Staff and customers from your server: POST /v1/users creates an active user { name, email?, phone?, role?, password?, addresses?, notes?, custom? } and sends nothing (an email address or a phone number is needed); PATCH /v1/users/:id also changes email and phone (normalized, unique, marked verified; null removes one), password (the user is signed out everywhere), addresses and twoStep: false (turns another user's two-step sign-in off, for example when its secret can no longer be read; they set it up again); DELETE /v1/users/:id { reason } erases the user at once here and in every connected product; DELETE /v1/users/:id?scope=accounts removes them from Accounts only (the user, their sessions and codes) and every other product keeps its data: use it to remove someone from your team. Add user and invites make an account that signs in by its email address when it has one, else by its phone number (Forgot password by email follows it). Answers carry hasPassword, roleSince, lockedUntil and recoveryCodesLeft. GET /v1/users?permission=<product>:<key>&blocked=false lists the unblocked users whose role grants a permission (products' staff alerts read it). Guards, always, when the call comes with a signed-in staff member (SS-Sign-In next to the server token) or a ticket: nobody changes their own role, blocks or deletes themselves; nobody edits, blocks or deletes a user whose role ranks above theirs, or gives a role ranking above theirs; the last unblocked Owner is never demoted, blocked or deleted (403 forbidden). Without an acting user your server token stays all-powerful.
serverSignIn: Sign-in from your server: every sign-in, sign-up, code, renew and sign-out route also takes your server token with the visitor's address in SS-Visitor-IP (required on writes; it drives the per-visitor limits and the risk checks) and, optionally, the visitor's browser in SS-Visitor-Agent (the device list names it). The answer carries the refresh token in the body for your server to keep; renew with POST /v1/session/refresh. Routes of a signed-in user take the sign-in in SS-Sign-In as usual.
imported: Passwords from another system (importers): bcrypt hashes ($2a$, $2b$, $2y$, any cost) and PBKDF2 hashes written as pbkdf2$<iterations>$<salt>$<hash> (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 of <pepper>:<password>, base64) sign in as they are; paste that system's pepper into Connections → Pepper of imported passwords. After the first good sign-in the password is saved the Accounts way. Imported two-step sign-in keeps its authenticator secret, and its old recovery codes (sha256 of recovery: and the code) each work once.
install: Add the script to the pages of your website and place the visitor widgets where they should appear: sign_in, my_account, and role_request (Role requests: visitors ask for a role, for example membership). The sign-in widget also takes setup links (?ss_setup=<code> on its page). Widgets render nothing while their features are off or the product is stopped.
admin: Admin widgets run in your own admin with a ticket. Users (users.read to see, users.manage to change): status chips with their counts, search and filters (tags too), saved views (open, save the filters as a view, rename, reorder and delete them), each user's detail, Add user, Edit (contacts, password, notes, custom fields, addresses), Invite (sent, or the link handed to you), and in its More menu a sign-in code and a setup link (Staff sign-in codes and setup links), sign out everywhere, approve or decline a sign-up, keep or delete on a deletion request, block, and Delete user behind a typed confirmation (or remove them from Accounts only, keeping their data in your other products); with Role requests on, the requests list with invite, a new link for an invited request, decline (pending or invited) and open again. Roles (roles.manage). Activity (activity.read, Activity log copy): every product's copies with counts per product and filters. Include the script without data-token, place the widgets and register your ticket function. The widget calls it at start and 1 minute before the ticket expires; your server checks the user's sign-in and role every time.
tickets: Your server asks for a ticket with the server token (never send the server token to a browser). The origin is the address of your admin page: any https origin, or a local one while testing. Tickets last 15 minutes and carry only the permissions of switched-on features.
business: Every product reads your business basics from https://<your domain>/.well-known/business.json. Only name is required; without the file the name is your domain and the time zone is UTC.
api: Routes answer JSON, or nothing where the reference shows no answer (204, and 202 for Forgot password); errors are RFC 9457 problems with a stable code (a refused field is named in errors[0].path), and our widgets show your own texts for them, never the English detail. The users, role requests and activity copies are paged with cursor and limit, newest first. Routes of a feature that is off answer 403 feature_off. The reference below gives each route's body, query parameters and answer; our tests check every answer against it.

phone_password: Routes: POST /v1/sign-up/phone-password, POST /v1/sign-in/phone-password { phone, password, remember }, POST /v1/password/phone/forgot { phone } and POST /v1/password/phone/reset { phone, code, password }. PUT /v1/me/password also serves users with a phone number. Settings: visitors can sign up (off: only you give passwords, through Add user, setup links and invites; sign-up answers sign_up_closed), minimum length (6–128), maximum length (128–256), letter and digit, breached-password check, wrong passwords before a lock, the lock, the quiet hours after which wrong passwords are forgotten (1–720, default 24), Forgot password (code or off) and the Forgot password page.
staff_links: POST /v1/users/:id/sign-in-code answers { code, expiresAt }: 6 digits for staff to read to the user, never sent, single use, typed into the phone-code, email-code or phone + password screen; a new one cancels the old. POST /v1/users/:id/setup-link answers { url, expiresAt }: it lets the user choose a password (also without an email address) through POST /v1/setup-links/accept { code, password }, which signs them in; using the link proves the user's phone number (you send the link to it, so their guest orders and points join the account) and signs their other devices out. Set your setup page with {code} (for example https://www.example.com/account/setup/{code}); without one the link opens your website with ?ss_setup=, which the sign-in widget takes. Before the password, a setup page can ask POST /v1/setup-links/lookup { code } (the code in the body, so it stays out of addresses and request logs): valid with the person's display name, the last 4 digits of their phone number and when the link ends (to greet them), else expired, used, canceled (a newer link replaced it, or its request was declined) or invalid (an unknown or wrong code, which learns nothing); the sign-in widget greets by name and says why a link no longer works. POST /v1/users/invite takes deliver: return to answer the invite link instead of sending it. Each is logged with the acting user.
role_requests: Visitors ask with POST /v1/role-requests { role, name, phone | email, note } (no account; the roles you list in Settings). A repeat ask changes nothing. Privacy first: with revealStatus off (the default) every ask answers the same outcome requested, in about the same time, so nobody who types someone's phone number or email address learns whether it belongs to a member or has a request or invite; the role request widget shows one text that fits everyone (request.received). Switch revealStatus on only when your visitors should hear what is already there (for example, your earlier website told them), knowing anyone can then check a number or address: then a new request answers requested with its id, and a repeat ask already_member (the user holding that proven phone number, else email address, has the role), already_requested (it waits for your staff), already_invited (its setup link still works) or invite_expired (its link ran out), for your page's own words, and the widget words each (request.sent, request.alreadyRequested, request.alreadyInvited, request.inviteExpired, request.alreadyMember; edit any of these texts). Your server and the Users widget read GET /v1/role-requests?status=pending|invited|completed|declined|expired (with counts) and one request by its id with GET /v1/role-requests/<id> (the Users widget: GET /v1/admin/role-requests/<id>, with the permission of the list; 404 not_found for an unknown id), and POST /v1/role-requests/:id/invite (creates the user, or finds the user with that phone or email, and answers a setup link unless they already have a password; a user who never proved that phone or email gets nothing and the invite answers 409 contact_unverified until you check with the person, confirm it on their user or remove that account; a user has one role, so a request never lowers one: for a user whose role ranks above the request's, for example staff asking with their own phone number, the invite answers 409 conflict and you change the role on their user if that is what you want), /setup-link (a new link for an invited request whose link still works or ran out; the old one stops working), /decline (a pending or invited request: its link stops working, a user the invite created who never signed in is removed, else the role the invite gave goes back to the one before) and /reopen. Settings: revealStatus (off by default, above) and giveRoleAt (invite, the default: the role is given when staff invite; completion: when the person sets their password with the setup link, so they hold the role only once they finish). A request is completed when the password is set or the role given; expired when its setup link ran out. Users carry roleSince (Member since).
import: Moving in from another system (ss-import, server token): POST /v1/import/roles, /fields, /users, /requests and /copies take NDJSON of Accounts' own record shapes with their ids, at most 1,000 records or 4 MB a call (?dryRun=1 checks without writing and reports every refused line; a record replaces the stored one with its key, and an unknown field, websiteId too, refuses it by name); /v1/import/:collection/prune removes records an import wrote that the source no longer has (never records made in Accounts itself); POST /v1/import/finish and GET /v1/import/status (counts and sums). Import roles first: a user's role must exist. A user's roleSince defaults to its createdAt; passwordChangedAt (when the password was last changed in the source, optional) ends the sessions made before it; a user or request without createdAt keeps the one stored, else gets the time of the import. Users keep their password hashes (bcrypt, pbkdf2$ with the Pepper of imported passwords connection, scrypt$) and their two-step secrets, sealed at once; an email address or phone number another user holds is refused. Nothing is sent. Switch the feature off once the import is verified.

build.phone_code:
Add a sign-in page with the widget script (data-token: your browser token) and
, and a My account page with
. Paste your Notifications server token into Connections; codes by WhatsApp also need your WhatsApp template approved at Meta. On your own screens instead: POST /v1/sign-in/phone/code { phone }, then POST /v1/sign-in/phone { phone, code }. Your server checks sign-ins offline with the public keys (/v1/websites//keys).
build.phone_password:
Add a sign-in page with the widget script (data-token: your browser token) and
, and a My account page with
. Forgot password sends a code through Notifications (paste its server token into Connections); with it off in Settings, its link opens your Forgot password page. On your own screens instead: POST /v1/sign-up/phone-password, POST /v1/sign-in/phone-password { phone, password }, POST /v1/password/phone/forgot and POST /v1/password/phone/reset. Your server checks sign-ins offline with the public keys (/v1/websites//keys).
build.email_password:
Add a sign-in page with the widget script (data-token: your browser token) and
, and a My account page with
; reset links open the page that asked (list your other hosts in Settings, resetHosts). Paste your Notifications server token into Connections. On your own screens instead: POST /v1/sign-up/password, POST /v1/sign-in/password, POST /v1/password/forgot { email, returnTo }, and on the returnTo page POST /v1/password/reset with the #ss_accounts_reset value as token. Your server checks sign-ins offline with the public keys (/v1/websites//keys).
build.email_code:
Add a sign-in page with the widget script (data-token: your browser token) and
, and a My account page with
; magic links open the page that asked. Paste your Notifications server token into Connections. On your own screens instead: POST /v1/sign-in/email/code { email, returnTo }, then POST /v1/sign-in/email with { email, code }, or with { link } (the #ss_accounts_link value) on the returnTo page. Your server checks sign-ins offline with the public keys (/v1/websites//keys).
build.google:
In your Google OAuth client, add the return address shown in Connections (/oauth/google/callback on Accounts' address) as an authorized redirect URI, and paste the client ID and secret into Connections. Place
and
on your sign-in and My account pages with the widget script (data-token: your browser token). On your own screens instead: POST /v1/sign-in/google/start { returnTo }, open its url, then on the returnTo page POST /v1/sign-in/exchange with the #ss_accounts_code value as code. Your server checks sign-ins offline with the public keys (/v1/websites//keys).
build.apple:
In your Apple Services ID, add the return address shown in Connections (/oauth/apple/callback on Accounts' address) as a Return URL, with its domain, and paste the Services ID, Team ID, Key ID and .p8 private key into Connections. Place
and
on your sign-in and My account pages with the widget script (data-token: your browser token). On your own screens instead: POST /v1/sign-in/apple/start { returnTo }, open its url, then on the returnTo page POST /v1/sign-in/exchange with the #ss_accounts_code value as code. Your server checks sign-ins offline with the public keys (/v1/websites//keys).
build.facebook:
In your Facebook app (Facebook Login), add the return address shown in Connections (/oauth/facebook/callback on Accounts' address) as a valid OAuth redirect URI, and paste the App ID and App secret into Connections. Place
and
on your sign-in and My account pages with the widget script (data-token: your browser token). On your own screens instead: POST /v1/sign-in/facebook/start { returnTo }, open its url, then on the returnTo page POST /v1/sign-in/exchange with the #ss_accounts_code value as code. Your server checks sign-ins offline with the public keys (/v1/websites//keys).
build.roles:
In your admin, place
and
with the widget script (no data-token) and SSAccounts.admin({ getTicket }); your getTicket route checks the user's sign-in, role and permissions, then asks POST /v1/tickets with your server token. Paste your other products' server tokens into Connections so roles can grant their permissions. Your server can also use /v1/users and /v1/roles, and reads role and permissions from each sign-in.
build.custom_fields: Add your fields in the Accounts dashboard (Custom fields): the sign-in and My account widgets ask for them at sign-up and in My account. On your own screens, send them as custom with the sign-up and with PATCH /v1/me; your server reads and changes them through /v1/users (custom).
build.two_step: Nothing extra with the widgets: the sign-in widget asks for the code, and My account sets two-step up and makes new recovery codes. On your own screens, a sign-in that answers status two_step or two_step_setup goes on with POST /v1/sign-in/two-step { challenge, code or recoveryCode }, and My account uses POST /v1/me/two-step/setup, /enable, /disable and /recovery-codes. To require it, set two-step to required on the role (Roles and permissions).
build.approval: Choose who can sign up in Settings, and set the invite page: a page of your website with the sign-in widget, where invite links open. Invites go out through Notifications (paste its server token into Connections); send them and approve or decline waiting sign-ups in the Users admin widget, or from your server with POST /v1/users/invite and POST /v1/users/<id>/approve or /decline. On your own screens, a sign-up may answer { status: pending }, and your invite page sends the #ss_accounts_invite value as token to POST /v1/invites/accept.
build.risk_checks: Nothing on your pages: the widgets send their device id. On your own screens, send deviceId (a random id the browser keeps, 16 to 64 letters, digits, - or _) with each sign-up so accounts per device can be counted; sign-ups made from your server send the visitor's address in SS-Visitor-IP.
build.consents: Set your consent list in the dashboard (Settings → Consents; your terms are there from the start: add their page and change the version when they change), for example your terms, your privacy policy and offers by email: each has your words, a page to read, a version, required or not, and a purpose — agreement, or marketing, which is kept apart (never required; users give or withdraw it in My account). The sign-in widget shows the boxes at sign-up and, when a required one changed, before the sign-in goes on; My account lists them all. On your own screens, send consents: { key: true } with the sign-up or sign-in for the boxes the visitor checked (a required agreement not given in its current version answers 403 consent_required with the consents still asked), and a signed-in user gives or withdraws them with POST /v1/me/consents { consents: { key: true or false } }. Your server reads the list with GET /v1/consents and finds the users who give one with GET /v1/users?consent=<key>.
build.data_rights:
Nothing extra on your pages: My account (
) has Download my data and Delete my account; on your own screens, call POST /v1/me/export and POST /v1/me/delete. Paste your other products' server tokens into Connections so both reach them. Approve deletions in the Users admin widget or with POST /v1/users//deletion/approve, or set in Settings the days after which they go ahead.
build.activity_copies:
Nothing on your pages: paste this website's Accounts server token into Connections in each of your other products. Read the copies in your admin with
(the widget script, SSAccounts.admin and a ticket with activity.read), or from your server with GET /v1/activity-copies.
build.orders_tab:
Nothing extra on your pages: paste your Ecommerce server token into Connections, and My account (
) shows the user's last 20 orders. On your own screens, read them with GET /v1/me/orders (your browser token and the sign-in in SS-Sign-In).
build.staff_links: Set your setup page in Settings: the page with the sign-in widget, or your own page with {code} in its address that calls POST /v1/setup-links/lookup { code } and POST /v1/setup-links/accept { code, password }; without one, setup links open your home page with ?ss_setup=, so place the sign-in widget there. Staff make codes and links in the Users admin widget (More menu), or your server with POST /v1/users/<id>/sign-in-code and POST /v1/users/<id>/setup-link.
build.role_requests:
Add a page with
and the widget script (data-token: your browser token), or your own form that calls POST /v1/role-requests { role, name, phone or email, note }, and list the roles visitors may ask for in Settings. Staff answer in the Users admin widget, or your server with GET /v1/role-requests and POST /v1/role-requests//invite or /decline; an invite answers a setup link for the person, which opens the setup page of Staff sign-in codes and setup links (else your home page with ?ss_setup=).
build.import: Nothing on your pages: run ss-import with this website's Accounts server token; it sends roles, custom fields, users, role requests and activity history to POST /v1/import/<collection> (?dryRun=1 checks first) and compares them with GET /v1/import/status. Imported pbkdf2$ password hashes need that system's pepper in Connections (Pepper of imported passwords). Switch Import off once the import is verified.
